item.title: Dozens dead in Spain after high-speed train slams into another stopped on tracks
item.description:
Spanish transport minister suggests an ‘inexplicable’ traffic order preceded the crash Full report from Spain At least 30 people are believed to have died after two high-speed trains collided in the province of Toledo in Spain, with concerns the death toll could be much higher. The number of people affected is expected to rise ( 10:46 ) , local authorities said, with growing concerns about a “major tragedy” ( 11:03 ). The affected trains are understood to be Iryo 7076 with 146 passengers plus one baby on board, and AVE 2080 with 397 passengers on board, making it 544 people in total on board of both train ( 11:00 ). The incident comes less than a year after a similar crash in Adamuz, the province of Córdoba, which killed 46 and injured 152 in January this year ( 11:00 ). Spain’s high-speed railway network ranks as the largest in Europe and the second biggest in the world after China,…

item.title: Israel election results live: Netanyahu bloc and main opposition set to fall short of majority as 92% of ballots counted
item.description:
In the frantic hours after Israelis cast their ballots on Tuesday, early exit polls briefly suggested that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s reign might finally be coming to an end. But as official tallies filtered into Wednesday morning, political reality emerged: while Netanyahu fell short of an outright parliamentary majority, he remains firmly in control of Israel’s political destiny. With roughly 71-77% of the ballots counted in the election for the 26th Knesset, the Central Elections Committee reported that Netanyahu’s Right-wing and religious alliance stood at around 54 seats, which is short of the 61 required for a majority in the 120-seat legislature. The primary opposition, the anti-Netanyahu “change bloc” led by former military chief of staff Gadi Eisenkot, lagged further behind at roughly 47 seats, even with turnout surging to 77.7%, Israel’s highest since 1999. item.title: Who Said It: Marissa Mayer, or Odysseus?
item.description:
Late last year, Marissa Mayer was struggling with what felt like an impossible task. Her daughter Marielle was turning 10, and Marielle’s teacher wanted three bullet points summarizing what made her special. Mayer—the former chief executive of Yahoo and a pioneer at Google, where she was the first female engineer—likes cracking a hard problem. But she felt overwhelmed by the range and complexity of potential answers. So Mayer asked her personal A.I. assistant, Dazzle. Within a few seconds, Dazzle delivered an answer. “It came back and was like, your daughter is empathetic, creative and an animal lover,” Mayer said. She thought it was perfect. In an attempt to express the blend of bewilderment and despair brought on by this New York Times anecdote , I have concocted a quiz: Which is it—a question the tech industry wants me to ask AI, or something Odysseus asks upon returning to Ithaca…

item.title: New poll shows billionaire tax falling behind as election nears
item.description:
A “Tax the Ultra-Rich Now” bus parked in San Francisco on Oct. 3, 2026. Photo by Manuel Orbegozo for CalMatters Californians’ appetite for a first-in-the-nation wealth tax appears to be waning. With less than a week before Election Day, support for Proposition 40 , a proposed billionaire tax, is now under water, according to the latest poll by Public Policy Institute of California . Published Tuesday, the survey found that 46% of 1,086 likely voters support the tax, while 52% don’t. That’s a notable change from last month, when Prop. 40 proponents held a slim 52% majority. The billionaire tax is by far the biggest and most expensive fight on the ballot. As of mid-October, wealthy people who oppose it have raised more than $205 million to fight the tax, including Google co-founder Sergey Brin, who has poured at least $102 million. item.title: Cyclone leaves trail of destruction in India as thousands evacuated
item.description:
A 125-kilometer-per-hour cyclone hit the southeastern coast of India on Wednesday, October 28, as authorities warned of localised flooding and the uprooting of power and communications poles. At least 180,000 people have been evacuated, while neighbouring Sri Lanka and Nepal have also issued weather warnings. Camille Corcoran reports.
